paragraphs.text: A homily by Saint John Chrysostom on the Annunciation to the Mother of God. Once again, good news of joy. Once again, an announcement of freedom. Once again, a calling back; once again, a return. Once again, gladness.

Once again, deliverance from slavery. An angel speaks with a virgin, because the serpent spoke to a woman. "In the sixth month," he said, "the angel Gabriel was sent from God to a virgin betrothed to a man." Gabriel was sent to announce salvation to the whole world. Gabriel was sent, carrying to Adam the writ of his recall. Gabriel was sent to a virgin, to turn the dishonor of womankind into honor. Gabriel was sent, to prepare a fitting bridal chamber for the pure bridegroom. Gabriel was sent to betroth creation to the one who created it. Gabriel was sent to the living palace of the King of angels. Gabriel was sent to a virgin betrothed to Joseph but kept for Jesus. A bodiless servant was sent to an undefiled handmaid. One free from sin was sent to her who admits no corruption. A lamp was sent, announcing the Sun of righteousness. The dawn was sent, going before the light of day. Gabriel was sent, announcing the one who is in the Father's bosom and in his mother's arms. Gabriel was sent to proclaim the one who is on the throne and in the cave. Gabriel was sent, announcing a royal mystery that is known,

but not investigated; a mystery that is revered, but not measured; a mystery spoken of in theology, but not investigated; a mystery confessed, but not measured. In the sixth month Gabriel was sent to a virgin. But which sixth month? And he says: Which one? From the time Elizabeth received the good news, from the time she conceived John. How, then, is this clear? Let the archangel himself tell you, speaking to the virgin: "And behold," he said, "Elizabeth your relative has also conceived a son, and this is the sixth month for her who was called barren." He said, "In the sixth month," for this is the sixth month since John's conception. For the soldier had to precede the commander; the herald had to come first, before the Lord's arrival. So in the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent to a virgin. Betrothed to a man, but not united with him; entrusted to Joseph, but kept for Jesus. Why was she entrusted to him? So that the deceiver would not immediately discover the mystery. For the evil one knew that the King would come from a virgin, since he too had heard Isaiah’s words, when he said, “Behold, the virgin will conceive in her womb and bear a son.” And he kept a most careful watch over what had been proclaimed about the virgin, so that when he learned that this mystery was being fulfilled, then the prophet would prepare [?]. For this

reason the Master came forth from a betrothed woman, to remain hidden from the deceiver. For a betrothed woman is bound to another. In the sixth month, Gabriel the archangel was sent to a virgin betrothed to a man whose name was Joseph. Hear, then, what the prophet said to you about this man and about the virgin. “A sealed book,” he said, “will be given to a man who knows how to read.” What, then, is this sealed book? The blameless virgin. And by whom will it be given? By the priests, clearly. And to whom? Is it not to this carpenter Joseph? For this Joseph, brothers, had previously entered an honorable marriage and fathered sons, but he lost his wife and lived in chastity, bringing up his children in the discipline and instruction of the Lord. So, when the apostle Paul came to preach and found one of this man’s sons, he wrote, “I saw none of the other apostles, except James, the Lord’s brother”—not because he was born of Mary, but because he was born of Joseph. Since, then, the priests betrothed Mary to Joseph as a chaste man and entrusted her to him while awaiting the time for marriage, it was fitting for one who had received her in this way to keep the virgin undefiled. For long beforehand the prophet proclaimed this: “A sealed book,” he said, “will be given

to a man who knows how to read”—that is, one who has been married—“and he will say, ‘I cannot read it.’” Why, then, can you not read it, Joseph? “I cannot read it,” he said, “because the book is sealed.” For whom, then, is it being kept? For the Creator of all. It is being kept as a dwelling. But let us turn to what lies before us. In the sixth month, the angel Gabriel was sent to a virgin, having received these commands: “Go, then,” he said, “O angel. Be a servant of an awesome mystery; minister to a hidden wonder. In my compassion I wish to come down in search of Adam, who has gone astray. The one created in my image has been aged by sin—the one made in my likeness. The work of my hands [?] has grown dark. The beauty that I created—the wolf is devouring what I have nurtured. Paradise has lost its inhabitant. The tree of life is guarded by a flaming weapon. The gates of the place of nourishment have closed. I have compassion on the defeated one. And I wish to grapple with the adversary. I wish to conceal myself from the heavenly powers. To you alone I reveal this secret. Go to the virgin Mary. Go to the living city, of which the prophet said: Glorious things have been spoken of you, O city.

Go to my paradise endowed with reason. Go to my eastern gate. Go to the dwelling worthy of my Word. Go to the second heaven on earth. Go to the vast cloud. Announce to her the dew of my coming. Go to the holy place prepared for me. Go to my chosen, honored temple. Go to the pure bride of my birth in the flesh. Speak into the ears of the ark endowed with reason. Prepare an entrance for me through her hearing. But do not make a clamor or trouble the virgin’s soul. Appear gently before the sanctuary. With your first words, proclaim joy to her. Say to Mary: Rejoice, favored one, so that I may have mercy on Eve, who has suffered. Hearing this, the angel pondered within himself, thinking as was fitting: What is being spoken of is a wondrous deed beyond understanding. He who is fearsome to the cherubim and invisible to the seraphim, who is beyond the understanding of the angelic powers, himself promises the virgin to reveal his coming in person. Indeed, he promises her an entrance through her hearing. And he who condemned Eve is coming to glorify his daughter greatly. He says: Prepare an entrance for me through her hearing. Can a womb, then, contain the uncontainable? Truly, a wondrous miracle of what is hidden! Truly, a fearful

mystery! While the angel was pondering such things, the Master said to him: Why are you troubled and amazed, Gabriel? Were you not sent by me before to Zechariah the priest? Did you not give him the good news of John’s birth? And when the priest did not believe, you brought silence upon him. Did you not condemn the old man to speechlessness? And was it not you who spoke, while I confirmed it? Did not the deed follow your announcement of the good news? Has not the barren woman conceived? Has not her womb obeyed? Has not the affliction of barrenness departed? Has not nature’s inertia fled? Is she not now producing an ear of grain? Has not the childless woman given birth? Can it not be accomplished by me, who made everything with a word? Why did you fall into doubt? And what did the angel say in reply? “Master, to heal the impediments of nature, to loosen dreadful bonds, to call deadened limbs back to the power of life, to command the body to hasten in bearing children, to undo the barrenness of aged limbs, to transform an aged reed into its youthful form, to make barren earth suddenly appear as a mother of sheaves—this is the work of your power,

performed as a matter of course. Sarah bears witness, and Rebekah with her, and Anna too, who were enslaved to the affliction of bitter barrenness and received freedom from you. But for a virgin to give birth without having intercourse with a man is beyond this bodily law. And you decree your coming to the maiden. The bounds of heaven and earth cannot contain you, Master. How, then, will a virgin’s womb contain you?” The Master again said to the angel, “Then how did Abraham’s tent contain me?” The angel said, “Because he possessed an ocean of hospitality. Yet there, Master, you appeared to the patriarch in his roadside tent and passed on, filling all things. And how will Mary bear the fire of your divinity? Your throne shines, bathed in radiance, and can you be borne by a frightened maiden?” The Master said to him, “Indeed, if the fire harmed the bush in the wilderness, then my coming will harm Mary too. But if that fire, a shadow [?], the coming of God’s fire from heaven, watered the bush and did not burn it, what then will you say of the reality, which descends not in a fiery flame but in the form of rain?” Then the angel carried out his command and, entering where the virgin was, cried out, saying, “Rejoice, favored one!

The Lord is with you. The devil will no longer prevail against you. For where the adversary first began his attack, there the physician first applies his medicine. From where death first came forth, there life made its life-giving entrance.” Through a woman evil grew, and through a woman better things flow forth. Rejoice, you who are favored. Do not be ashamed as though you were subject to condemnation, for by grace you become a mother to the condemned. Rejoice, favored bride and pure mother to the whole world laid waste. Rejoice, you who drowned a mother's death in your womb. Rejoice, living temple of God. Rejoice, shared dwelling of heaven and earth. Rejoice, spacious dwelling of the inseparable nature. With things thus, the physician came to the sick. To those sitting in darkness the sun of righteousness appeared; to those tossed by waves, calm. And an untroubled harbor, unchanging. For slaves who hate utterly, a mediator was born, and a bond of peace. For captive slaves, a deliverer; for those struggling with love, a strong protection came. For he is our peace, whom may we be deemed worthy to enjoy always, by the grace of Christ himself, to whom be glory and might forever and ever. Amen.
